defects: All 12.4 s are one continuous shot. Scenes change only by in-place dissolves, so there is no cut, camera move or change of scale between the three sections.
The pen-tip dot traces the spiral and the curve at a near-linear rate. Nothing accelerates, settles or overshoots, so the line has no weight.
The headline and body copy fade in and then hold still while only the line moves. Seconds 1–3 and 9–11 are close to dead air (measured change 0.6–1.7 and 0.8–1.0).

Moving from the one-year arc to the 68-year spiral, and from the spiral to the Keeling curve, is done with a crossfade. The spiral never unwinds into the time series, which is the obvious match-transform.
The source line and axis labels are around 6–8 px. They are unreadable at 1080 and will block up after compression.
At 100% the dense spiral rings show slight moiré and stepping where thin strokes sit closer than 2 px apart. The strokes are flat, with no glow and no change in thickness.
The '426.1' callout and the per-decade '+x.x' annotations crowd the top-right of the Keeling curve and sit close to the data line.

The audio is short tonal plucks with a few stacked harmonics over a low pad. It drops to silence at about 3.3 s, 6.6 s and 10 s, which reads as separate cues joined at the scene changes rather than one designed score.
gaps: The motion is not choreographed. Each scene does one thing: a line draws at constant speed, then the scene dissolves. Top studio work would give the line breath-like easing (inhale and exhale timing on the seasonal wobble), let the year counter accelerate through the decades, and transform the spiral physically into the Keeling curve. The piece's single idea needs that continuous transformation as its centrepiece.

The sound is simple synth plucks in three separate sections, with silent gaps at the scene changes. There is no designed breath sound, no layer that builds as the rings stack up, and no hit when the spiral reaches 2026. The audio follows the structure but adds no weight or emotion.

The finish is flat vector work. The lines have no light, depth, bloom or variation in thickness, and the micro-type is too small for screen. It reads as a well-styled interactive chart recorded to video rather than a finished film.
